blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Account deletion keeps the member's personal data in `users`) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: "UPDATE users SET deleted_at = datetime('now'), password_hash = NULL WHERE id = ?",
findings.recommendation: Erase the personal columns of the row on deletion (GDPR Art. 17, Art. 5(1)(c) and (e)): overwrite or null `email`, `display_name`, `phone` and `postal_address` (app/schema.sql:3-6) — `email` is NOT NULL UNIQUE, so replace it with an opaque placeholder such as `deleted-<id>@invalid` — keeping only the id that `orders.user_id` references, so orders stay for accounting without personal data as the proposal promises. Add a test asserting these columns no longer hold the member's values after `delete_account`; the current tests only check sign-in and sessions. State how backups are purged or expire.
findings.title: Account deletion keeps the member's personal data in `users`

findings.recommendation: `analytics_id` is added with no caller in the change; a salted hash with one global, permanent salt is pseudonymous personal data (GDPR Recital 26), not anonymous, so events carrying it stay linkable to the member after deletion. Either drop it from this change, or state where those analytics events go (processor, retention) and how `delete_account` erases them or breaks the link (e.g. a per-user salt deleted with the account).
findings.title: Pseudonymous analytics id survives erasure and has no use in the change
